nationalConstructionCode.reference: National Construction Code (NCC) / Building Code of Australia (BCA)
nationalConstructionCode.relevanceToFurniture: Furniture does not require building approval, but layout choices must not compromise the compliant design of the tenancy — particularly egress, accessibility, fire zones, and wet area boundaries

tenancyFitoutCompliance.buildingApproval: Major fit-out works (partitions, electrical, plumbing, fire systems) require Development Approval or Building Permit — furniture-only fit-outs typically do not
tenancyFitoutCompliance.landlordApproval: Always confirm tenant fit-out obligations in the lease — many leases require landlord written consent for any physical change, including furniture layout if it affects services
tenancyFitoutCompliance.ceilingAndServicesClearance: Furniture must not obstruct sprinkler heads, smoke detectors, HVAC diffusers, or emergency lighting — check ceiling layout before finalising furniture positions

fireCodeCompliance.egress: Egress paths must remain clear at all times — furniture positioning must maintain compliant egress widths (min 1,000mm general; 1,200mm egress routes)
fireCodeCompliance.furnitureMaterials: Commercial-grade furniture should use fire-retardant or fire-resistant materials where specified by tenancy fitout rules — check building-specific requirements
fireCodeCompliance.storageFurniture: High storage units (above 1.8m) positioned near sprinkler heads may affect sprinkler spray patterns — confirm positioning with base building manager if units exceed 1.8m height near sprinkler heads

accessibilityCompliance.relevantStandard: AS 1428 — Design for Access and Mobility

typicalRequirements.wheelchairClearance: 800mm clear floor space beside desks for wheelchair approach
typicalRequirements.deskHeight: 700–720mm fixed desk for accessible workstations; sit-stand preferred
typicalRequirements.receptionCounter: One section of reception counter at accessible height (750–900mm) per DDA requirements

accessibilityCompliance.DDA: Disability Discrimination Act 1992 requires reasonable adjustments in workplace design — applicable to new office fit-outs for employers with 5+ staff

stateSpecificNotes.Queensland: Brisbane City Council planning codes apply — check if project falls within Heritage Overlay or specific precinct rules for tenancy fit-outs
stateSpecificNotes.NewSouthWales: Sydney CBD buildings may have specific heritage or high-rise fit-out requirements — confirm with building management
stateSpecificNotes.Victoria: Melbourne City Council and Heritage Victoria overlays may apply in CBD heritage buildings
